sections.h2: Which offices deal with property tax in the City of Homestead?
sections.html:
Homestead lies inside Miami-Dade County, so the county's Office of the Tax Collector, at 200 NW 2nd Avenue in Miami, handles your bill. Reach it at 305-375-5448. The city levies its own rate, as do the School Board and other districts, but none of them mails or collects the bill.

Value and exemptions belong to the Property Appraiser, whose homestead line is 305-375-4712. Tax deed auctions belong to the Clerk of Courts and Comptroller.

The name causes confusion. "Homestead" is this South Florida city and also the Florida exemption for a primary residence, and the two have no automatic link: a Homestead city house must still file for the exemption, and homes across Miami-Dade can claim it too.

sections.h2: When do City of Homestead tax notices arrive and what do early payers save?
sections.html:
The collector's real estate page gives October 30, 2026 as the mailing date for 2026 notices, with online viewing and payment from that day. Payment without penalty runs through March 31.

Early payment discounts per the Florida Department of Revenue taxpayer page and the Miami-Dade Tax Collector FAQ
Month of paymentDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchGross tax

Checks mailed to the Miami address earn the discount by postmark. Banks' bill-pay services need about five business days, so schedule early and quote the folio number printed on the notice.

sections.h2: What follows a missed deadline in Homestead?
sections.html:
On April 1 the account is delinquent and picks up at least 3% interest plus advertising and fee charges. If 2026 tax is not paid before June 1, 2027, the collector says a certificate may issue, and that year's certificate sale is listed as starting June 1, 2027.

The collector warns that a certificate can end in loss of the property down the line. A holder can seek a tax deed after two years from April 1 of the issue year, and the clerk runs the auction. The high bidder leaves a deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is bigger, and settles in full, with stamps and recording costs, within 24 hours.

A local wrinkle: some Miami-Dade bills carry a Water, Road and Sewer assessment collected in 30-year annual installments. The collector states that such a bill must be paid by May 31 or a certificate is sold on the remaining lien balance. Look for that line on your notice.

sections.h2: How much of the bill can a Homestead exemption remove?
sections.html:
Up to $50,000 of assessed value comes off for a qualifying owner. The first $25,000 reaches every levy, and the second slice reduces only non-school levies on value above $50,000. You must live in the home on January 1 and get Form DR-501 to the Property Appraiser by March 1.

  • Renting the property or leaving Florida ends the exemption.
  • Save Our Homes caps yearly assessed growth at the smaller of 3 percent or the inflation number, shown as 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • A transfer of title restarts the property at just value the next January 1, apart from spouse and certain death transfers.
  • Portability moves part of the capped savings to a new Florida homestead, filed on DR-501T within three years of January 1 of the year the old homestead was left.

Buyers can try the Property Appraiser's online tax estimator before an offer.

sections.h2: What can a Homestead owner do about a value or exemption notice?
sections.html:
The Property Appraiser mails TRIM notices every August, and the Value Adjustment Board hears petitions filed within 25 days of that mailing. A denied exemption allows 30 days from the denial letter.

File the exemption on time so no appeal is needed. If a refund follows a Property Appraiser or board ruling, the collector's FAQ lists a refund email address for it. A refund arising from a sale is a different matter, handled between buyer and seller at closing.

sections.h2: What do City of Homestead budget announcements say about the rate?
sections.html:
The city announced on October 2, 2026 that its approved FY 2026 to 2027 budget keeps the operating millage rate unchanged from the year before. It does not print the number in that notice, so read the rate off your own notice.

The same announcement mentions $32 million for capital projects and five more police officer positions. Separately, voters were asked on November 4, 2025 to approve two general obligation bonds, one for parks and one for roads. The city's FAQ estimated 0.3661 mills for parks and 0.3983 mills for roadways if all of it were issued, and said borrowing would come in several series. Ask the city whether either bond now appears on your parcel.

Total millage on any parcel is the sum of every taxing district, and the collector's FAQ says to find it on the bill.

sections.h2: How do I pay, and where do I find older tax records?
sections.html:
The collector accepts payment online by check, credit card or debit card, in person by check, cashier's check, money order, certified funds, cash, cards or Apple Pay, and by mailed check. Write the folio number and a phone number on a mailed check, make it payable to the Miami-Dade County Office of the Tax Collector in U.S. funds, and leave out sensitive details.

  • Wire payments: email the collector's wire address listed on its FAQ page for instructions. The collector says a wire takes one to two business days to post.
  • Older bills: the collector says it can supply property tax records older than those online, and the FAQ lists an email address for the request.
  • Escrow: if you are unsure whether your lender is paying, ask the lender directly.
  • Roll changes: the certified tax roll reaches the collector once a year, expected around November 1, so recent ownership or address changes may not show online before then.

The collector's FAQ adds that Florida has no personal property tax on vehicles, which spares a seller who is also moving a car or boat from one more bill.

sections.h2: What should a Homestead seller prepare before closing?
sections.html:
Miami-Dade uses its own deed stamp rate, which the revenue department prints as 60 cents per $100 plus a 45-cent surtax, with the surtax skipped on a document transferring only a single-family dwelling. Most other counties charge 70 cents per $100. Every party to a document can be held liable.

  • Request a written payoff and ask about any delinquency or certificate notice.
  • Learn from the title company how the year will be apportioned.
  • Review the clerk's records for liens and check for a Water, Road and Sewer assessment.
  • Report any quarterly installment payments, since missing the July 31 first-payment cutoff removes the account from the plan.

When back taxes or a title problem would stall a bank-financed buyer, a cash purchase lets the title company clear the debt from proceeds.

faqs.q: Who bills a house in the City of Homestead?
faqs.a: The Miami-Dade County Office of the Tax Collector. The city sets a rate but does not send a bill.

faqs.q: When is Homestead real estate tax late?
faqs.a: After March 31. On April 1 the collector adds at least 3% interest, advertising costs and fees.

faqs.q: Does a tax certificate mean the city takes my house?
faqs.a: Not yet. It is a lien sold to an investor, and a tax deed application can follow two years after April 1 of the issue year.

faqs.q: Do I qualify for the exemption if I move in during the spring?
faqs.a: Not for that year. You need to live there on January 1 and apply by March 1. A sale also restarts the buyer's assessed value the following January 1.

faqs.q: Does the City of Homestead add its own transfer tax?
faqs.a: The city's pages do not list one, so confirm with the city. The state deed stamp tax applies at the Miami-Dade rate the revenue department prints.
